headline: Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang has said the United States must keep talking with Chinese AI companies because the technology could be dangerous.
score_reason: On-record remarks from a major industry figure on US-China AI safety; opinion, not policy, and read via relays.
importance_line: It feeds the debate on whether Washington and Beijing should coordinate on AI risk, but it is the view of one company executive, not a government position, and he has also argued against overly restrictive rules.
summary: CNBC reports, as relayed by Stocktwits and BigGo Finance, that Jensen Huang, chief executive of chipmaker Nvidia, told a London briefing on 14 Oct 2026 that the US "absolutely must" work with Chinese AI companies, describing AI as "powerful and potentially dangerous", and urged the UK to promote similar dialogue. He spoke after Nvidia announced $250 million over five years for UK AI safety and security research, and said the clash between US competition and China's protection of its own chipmakers would eventually have to be resolved.
notes: CNBC page blocked; read two relays that cite CNBC and Bloomberg interviews.
